evidence: The new RetentionName doc claimed to be 'the one rendering of a retention variant as a word' while store.go's retentionWord was a byte-identical rival namer, which the agent verified; it deleted retentionWord and routed formatIssueState through Frozen+RetentionName, so the comment became true rather than softened.
guidance_note: Before writing a doc comment that claims a function is 'the one' owner of a mapping, grep the repo for every existing switch over the same variants and migrate them in the same commit.

evidence: The collect guard widened from State()==StateClosed to !InPlay(), and the only cross-epic test covered the closed arm, which passed before the change; the agent added a frozen-side test plus a live-sides control and mutation-verified it.
guidance_note: When widening a predicate, add a test for each newly admitted variant at every call site the predicate guards, not just the site the ticket names.

evidence: The diff hunk shows the new test's doc comment appended directly after the history test's comment with no separator, so the two fused and the original function lost its doc; the agent moved the new test to the end of the file, one of the reviewer's offered remedies.
guidance_note: Insert new test functions at file end or between complete function boundaries, never between a doc comment and its function.

evidence: The changelog said the printIssueGroup test 'holds the status axis at open across all four arms' but the closed arm uses StateClosed by necessity, as the agent confirmed; wording was rescoped to 'both frozen arms'.
guidance_note: Check every quantified claim in a changelog entry ('all four arms') against the test table it describes before pushing.

evidence: RetentionName sat beside Frozen and RetentionTimestamps, both with dedicated table and impostor-panic tests, with none of its own; the agent added TestRetentionName and TestRetentionNameRefusesImpostors, and the F1 migration made the Live arm reachable.
guidance_note: When adding a function beside siblings that each have a table test and an impostor test, add the same pair for the new function in the same commit.

evidence: lifecycle.Retain takes a RetentionAction and has no close/open/start cases; the quoted 'cannot %s archived or deleted issue' refusals come from applyTransition's Frozen guard at store.go:89, which the agent verified and named instead.
guidance_note: When a changelog names the function responsible for a quoted error string, grep for the string's format to confirm the source before citing it.

narrative: Six round-0 findings, all real: one genuine duplicate-namer problem that contradicted the PR's own 'one owner' comment, two missing-test gaps, and three doc/changelog inaccuracies. The agent fixed all six in a single commit, chose to migrate rather than soften on F1, and round 1 came back with no findings. No fix caused a new finding.
guidance_observations: Half the findings were prose (changelog and comments) making claims about code that a grep would have refuted; a pre-push pass checking every factual claim in the changelog against the code would have removed them.
Batching every fix into one commit before re-review kept this to a single extra round.

evidence: The notice was derived from GetIssueDetail read before authorize, which can block on an untimed stdin prompt; the agent moved the claimant read after authorize (the reviewer's 'at minimum' remedy) and filed links-claims-3cey for deriving it from Apply's decision.
guidance_note: When a derived message depends on state read before an interactive wait, place the read after the wait in the original PR.

evidence: The agent reproduced 'claim transferred: alice -> alice' on a preset-assignee first start; the reviewer's Checkout.Present() fix broke TestRunTransitionStartClaimTransferEmitsNotice (a real pre-attribution transfer), so the agent added Claimant.Established/Held instead, which was right.
guidance_note: Before replacing a guard with a whole-struct zero-value comparison, list the reachable prior states (preset field with no event, event with no attribution) and test each one.

evidence: describeClaimant's both-halves branch was never asserted; the agent added an exact regex on the composed line in TestStartRefusesAndThenTakesOverAFreshForeignClaim and mutation-verified it by swapping the halves.
guidance_note: When adding a formatter with several render branches, assert each branch's exact output in at least one test.

evidence: Same defect as F2; the reviewer again proposed Checkout.Present(), which the agent showed misses pre-attribution holders, and the shared fix was Claimant.Established read by Held().
guidance_note: Before replacing a guard with a whole-struct zero-value comparison, list the reachable prior states (preset field with no event, event with no attribution) and test each one.

evidence: The agent narrowed GetIssueDetail to GetIssue+ListEvents but refused to read events only for start, calling that control-flow variability; in F18 it then gated the read on action.(model.Start) inside transferNotice, which is the reviewer's original suggestion, and that cost round 3.
guidance_note: When only one action consumes a read, scope the read to that consumer (for example a helper that type-asserts the action) rather than defending an unconditional read on uniformity grounds.

evidence: The memory engine's eventsFor scan is real but a pre-existing property of an in-process test engine; the proposed fix, falling back to the assignee for non-start actions in the storage no-op predicate, would bring back the two-spelling ownership predicate this PR removes. The agent declined it and filed links-storage-4hmy.

The comment's 'same pre-lock snapshot' claim was false (GetIssue at store.go:1077 and a separate listEvents query). The derived dropped-takeover failure does not hold: a no-op needs prior.Checkout == s.attribution, and a foreign write in the window can only make the latest establisher foreign. The agent fixed the comment and rebutted the race.
guidance_note: Do not write consistency guarantees ('same snapshot') into a comment without tracing where each value is read.

evidence: Same as F7, and the reviewer admitted it 'can't fully pin a deterministic worst-case sequence'. The equality asymmetry means a stale pair can only force a spurious write, never a false no-op, so the agent took the reviewer's own 'correct the comment' option.
guidance_note: Do not write consistency guarantees ('same snapshot') into a comment without tracing where each value is read.

evidence: Commit 859e9f0 (F2's fix) added Established and Held() to claimant.go and covered them only through the e2e test. The finding's headline case, the pre-attribution holder where Held() diverges from Derive, exists only because of that fix, although Claimant/After had been untested since the original commit. The agent added claimant_test.go with six killed mutations.
guidance_note: When a review fix adds a predicate to a pure package, add its direct table test in the same fix commit rather than relying on the e2e that found the bug.

evidence: F1's resolution conceded a residual read-vs-Apply window and filed links-claims-3cey, and 859e9f0 rewrote the store.go comment to admit it. The same commit edited the changelog paragraph but kept 'the notice prints exactly when a start recorded a transfer', which now contradicted the fix.
guidance_note: When a fix concedes a residual gap, grep the changelog and comments for absolute claims ('exactly', 'always') about that behavior and qualify them in the same commit.

evidence: ListEvents was added to IssueReader in 859e9f0 as F5's fix, with an ordering promise in its doc comment and two engine implementations, but no conformance case called it; the agent added one_issues_history_matches_the_whole_log and mutation-verified it on both engines.
guidance_note: When a fix adds a storage-contract method, add its conformance case in the same commit; the contract doc's promises are what the case must assert.

evidence: Round 2 reviewed 54d84ca, pushed for F10 before the planned claimant tests landed in 0695985; the reviewer correctly saw no tests, and the agent replied that 0695985 now adds them.
guidance_note: Do not push a partial fix commit that triggers a review round while planned fixes for other threads in the same round are still unpushed.

evidence: The ListEvents conformance case promised on F11 landed in 0695985 after round 2 reviewed 54d84ca, so the reviewer's grep correctly found no direct caller in tests.
guidance_note: Do not push a partial fix commit that triggers a review round while planned fixes for other threads in the same round are still unpushed.

evidence: This duplicates F12 within the same round. It is accurate for 54d84ca, and the tests landed afterward in 0695985.
guidance_note: Do not push a partial fix commit that triggers a review round while planned fixes for other threads in the same round are still unpushed.

evidence: 859e9f0's cli.go comment says Held is 'claims' own reading, the checkout and never the assignee', left over from the first attempt (Held = Checkout.Present()) on F2, while Held() returns c.Established. The flag names 54d84ca, but the drift was written in 859e9f0.
guidance_note: After abandoning a first-attempt fix, grep the comments written for that attempt and rewrite them to match the landed definition before pushing.

evidence: This is a third copy of the F12 finding in round 2. It is accurate for 54d84ca, and the agent pointed at 0695985.
guidance_note: Do not push a partial fix commit that triggers a review round while planned fixes for other threads in the same round are still unpushed.

evidence: This duplicates F13. The reviewer grepped 54d84ca's conformance.go and found only takeoverByANewCheckoutRecords, which was correct at that commit, and the case landed in 0695985.
guidance_note: Do not push a partial fix commit that triggers a review round while planned fixes for other threads in the same round are still unpushed.

evidence: F5's fix in 859e9f0 introduced an unconditional readClaimant for every runTransition verb, retention verbs included, although only the Start branch consumes it. The flag names e39e1ed, which only changed a comment. The agent moved the read into transferNotice behind action.(model.Start), going further than the reviewer and effectively adopting F5's rejected remedy.
guidance_note: When only one action consumes a read, scope the read to that consumer (for example a helper that type-asserts the action) rather than defending an unconditional read on uniformity grounds.

narrative: Round 0 raised eight substantive findings. The agent handled them well and correctly rejected the reviewer's Checkout.Present() fix on F2/F4 after a test caught it. Each fix commit then left gaps: no direct tests for the new Held/Established core or the new ListEvents contract method, a cli.go comment left over from the abandoned first attempt, a changelog 'exactly' contradicted by the conceded window, and an unconditional readClaimant. In round 2, five of six findings were re-reports, because 54d84ca was pushed before 0695985 carried the promised tests. F18 then undid the agent's own F5 pushback by gating the read on Start.
guidance_observations: Pushing a single-thread fix commit (54d84ca) while other planned fixes were still local caused a review round made mostly of duplicates; push all of a round's fixes together.
Every fix that adds a public surface (a method, a predicate, a contract entry) should carry its own direct test in the same commit; three of round 1's findings were exactly that omission.
When a first-attempt fix is abandoned mid-thread, sweep the comments and changelog text written for it; two findings were leftovers of superseded reasoning.
A law-backed pushback (dataflow-not-control-flow on F5) that the agent later reversed cost a round; check whether the 'uniform input' is consumed anywhere besides the one branch before defending it.

evidence: annotation.go registers four RoleBlocking kinds including NeedsDesign (line 109), but the changelog said three; the agent fixed the changelog, the backlog.go doc comment, and the PR body, but missed the backlog_test.go comment (see F3-F5).
guidance_note: Before writing a count of registry entries into prose, derive it from the registry, and when correcting a wrong count, grep the branch for every copy of the wrong phrasing.

evidence: This duplicates F1 on the same line: NeedsDesign was omitted from the RoleBlocking enumeration, and both threads were fixed together in 1dce91a.
guidance_note: Before writing a count of registry entries into prose, derive it from the registry, and when correcting a wrong count, grep the branch for every copy of the wrong phrasing.

evidence: 1dce91a corrected the 'three' count in the changelog and backlog.go but left backlog_test.go's 'two of the registry's three blocking kinds'. The agent deleted the count rather than correcting it, so the comment cannot drift again, and then swept the branch.
guidance_note: When correcting a wrong fact, grep the whole branch for the wrong phrasing ('three blocking kinds') and fix every hit before pushing; the agent did this sweep only after the second round.

evidence: This duplicates F3: the same stale 'three' in backlog_test.go that F1's fix missed, and the count was deleted in b92aaa6.
guidance_note: When correcting a wrong fact, grep the whole branch for the wrong phrasing ('three blocking kinds') and fix every hit before pushing; the agent did this sweep only after the second round.

evidence: This is a third copy of the same test-comment miscount left behind by 1dce91a, and it was resolved by the same deletion in b92aaa6.
guidance_note: When correcting a wrong fact, grep the whole branch for the wrong phrasing ('three blocking kinds') and fix every hit before pushing; the agent did this sweep only after the second round.

narrative: Round 0 flagged twice that the changelog miscounted RoleBlocking kinds (three instead of four). The agent's fix corrected three named copies of the wrong count but did not grep for others, so round 1 flagged the same miscount in a backlog_test.go comment three times. The final fix deleted the count from the test comment, which is a better fix, and swept the branch. Round 2 approved.
guidance_observations: The whole extra round came from correcting a repeated wrong fact by listing known sites instead of grepping for the phrasing; the branch-wide sweep the agent ran in round 2 belonged in round 1's fix.
Restating a registry count in several prose locations creates copies that drift; prose should name the fact a test pins rather than an arithmetic summary of another file.
